newsitem.title: USA: Palestinian official sees no peace progress.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian official sees no peace progress.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official said on Thursday that she expected little progress on stalled Middle East peace talks until the U.S. elections in November and called for a European role in the negotiations.
Hanan Ashrawi, a minister in the Palestinian National Authority and a member of the legislature, said "We do not expect much from a pre-election U.S. government."

She told the National Arab American Association that U.S. President Bill Clinton or Republican candidate Bob Dole "cannot take any positions even remotely critical of Israel" ahead of the Nov. 5 election.

Palestinian and Israeli negotiators resumed formal talks late on Wednesday at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Taba to implement a long-delayed Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
The United States has acted as a broker in the Israeli-Palestinian talks. The Israeli side has sounded notes of optimism that agreement is near but Palestinians have said they were at an impasse.
Ashrawi said that to make progress "I think the United States will have to take a more even-handed approach" and put pressure on Israel.
She said that the United States should accept a European presence in the negotiations, a step that Israel has long opposed, because of Europe's political and economic involvement in the region.

Ashrawi, who often serves as a spokeswoman in the United States for the Palestinians, accused Israel of conducting a "public relations campaign" while refusing to live up to previously negotiated agreements on Gaza and the West Bank.
"We have agreements that have flaws," she said, "but we have signed onto them."

She said the negotiations "have become hostage to this Israeli government." "At every meeting, the Israelis present modifications," she said, adding that "there is no positive feeling" among the negotiators.
